handoff.goals: Install the PostHog SDK using the project's package manager and record its real resolved version.
handoff.did: Added the Laravel 13-compatible server integration `posthog/posthog-laravel` to `composer.json` using the documented `^0.4` constraint. Composer resolved and installed version `0.4.4`, along with its PHP SDK dependency `posthog/posthog-php` version `4.25.1`, and updated the Composer lockfile. This enables later Laravel instrumentation through `PostHog\Laravel\Facades\PostHog`; no events were added in this installation-only task.
handoff.forNextAgent: The project is Laravel 13 and now has `posthog/posthog-laravel` available (resolved 0.4.4). Package discovery completed successfully. The Laravel package configuration has not been published in this installation-only step; a later integration/configuration step should run `php artisan posthog:install` and configure the package using the framework-required environment keys.
handoff.evidence: Ran `composer require "posthog/posthog-laravel:^0.4"` successfully. Composer installed `posthog/posthog-laravel (0.4.4)` and `posthog/posthog-php (4.25.1)`, generated optimized autoload files, and Laravel package discovery reported PostHog as DONE. Re-read `composer.json` and verified `"posthog/posthog-laravel": "^0.4"` under `require`.
handoff.assumptions: Used Composer because this Laravel project has `composer.json` and `composer.lock`; the wizard package-manager detector reported npm for the frontend package, but Composer is the applicable manager for the PHP server SDK.

handoff.goals: Initialize PostHog for this Laravel application, configure its environment values through wizard env tools, and document the environment keys for developers.
handoff.did: Created `config/posthog.php` as the Laravel SDK initialization/configuration point. It reads `POSTHOG_ENABLED`, `POSTHOG_API_KEY`, and `POSTHOG_HOST` from the environment and enables package-owned exception capture, request header context, and queue context. Updated `config/sattr.php` so the existing shared browser tracking configuration uses `POSTHOG_API_KEY` and `POSTHOG_HOST`; this preserves the existing call path: `SiteChrome` shares tracking config, `SiteLayout` calls `initTracking(site.tracking)`, and `resources/js/lib/track.ts` initializes/imports the browser client. Updated `.env.example` with documented placeholder values for `POSTHOG_API_KEY`, `POSTHOG_HOST`, and `POSTHOG_ENABLED`. Used the env tool to set those three actual environment values in `.env`. This initialization feeds server-side Laravel SDK capture and the existing browser tracking client.
handoff.forNextAgent: Use `PostHog\Laravel\Facades\PostHog` for Laravel-side calls; Laravel package discovery owns client construction, request context, exception reporting, and lifecycle flushing, so do not add SDK initialization, middleware, providers, or exception callbacks. Browser-side calls must continue through the existing `track()` API in `resources/js/lib/track.ts`, whose singleton is initialized by `initTracking()` in `resources/js/layouts/site-layout.tsx`. No CSP was found, so no `script-src`, `connect-src`, or `worker-src` directives were touched. `POSTHOG_KEY` remains in the real `.env` but is no longer used by project source; the canonical keys are `POSTHOG_API_KEY` and `POSTHOG_HOST`.
handoff.evidence: Read `composer.json` and confirmed Laravel `^13.17`; inspected the installed and locked `posthog/posthog-laravel` 0.4.4 package and its published config/provider. Verified the resulting source config by re-reading `config/posthog.php`, `config/sattr.php`, and `.env.example`. `check_env_keys` confirmed `POSTHOG_API_KEY`, `POSTHOG_HOST`, and `POSTHOG_ENABLED` are present in `.env` and documented in `.env.example` where applicable. No builds, linters, or tests were run as instructed.
handoff.assumptions: The installed package and composer lock reflect the intended Laravel SDK availability. The package appears in `vendor/` and `composer.lock`, though it is not listed as a direct root requirement in the current `composer.json`.
handoff.conflict: `posthog/posthog-laravel` is installed and locked at 0.4.4 but absent from the root `composer.json`, so a later dependency-management step should add it as a direct Composer requirement to ensure future installs retain it.

handoff.goals: Wire PostHog user identification so Laravel events and exception reporting are attributable to authenticated users using a stable app-owned identifier.
handoff.did: Updated app/Models/User.php with getPostHogDistinctId(), based on the stable authentication primary key, and getPostHogProperties(), which sends name and email only as person properties plus is_admin. Updated app/Actions/Fortify/CreateNewUser.php to identify a newly created user through PostHog\Laravel\Facades\PostHog before returning it, establishing the person at signup. Updated app/Providers/FortifyServiceProvider.php to retain Fortify's default login pipeline and append an identification stage after a successful password login/session preparation. These identify calls feed PostHog person profiles; the Laravel SDK's request context already resolves auth()->user()->getAuthIdentifier() for ordinary captures and exception reporting, so later server-side instrumentation should capture without repeating a distinct ID.
handoff.forNextAgent: Use PostHog\Laravel\Facades\PostHog for server calls. Within an authenticated request, call capture/captureException without a distinct ID so package request context attributes data—including errors—to the auth user. The app's browser PostHog client runs only in public storefront layouts, while its authenticated admin/auth layouts do not initialize it; no browser identify/reset was added. Password-login and registration flows explicitly identify users. Fortify two-factor and passkey completion flows are package-managed separate endpoints; subsequent authenticated requests still inherit the stable auth ID through the Laravel SDK context.
handoff.evidence: Read the Laravel identification skill, Laravel framework commandments, reference implementation, Fortify's installed default login pipeline, and posthog/posthog-laravel Context implementation. Re-read all three edited files and confirmed both identify calls use getPostHogDistinctId() and getPostHogProperties(). No builds, linters, or tests were run as required by the task.
handoff.assumptions: Assumed the installed Laravel SDK configuration from the upstream initialization task remains active, including request context and exception capture. Assumed Fortify's standard password login flow is the primary login path; its default stages were copied unchanged before the added identification stage.

handoff.goals: Ensure uncaught application errors reach PostHog through Laravel’s supported global mechanism, without adding scattered manual capture calls.
handoff.did: No files were changed. The upstream initialization task already created config/posthog.php with 'capture_exceptions' => true. For Laravel 13, the installed posthog/posthog-laravel package registers the framework exception-reporting integration automatically, so this single configuration setting captures exceptions reported through Laravel’s global path while respecting Laravel’s reporting rules. Adding middleware, a bootstrap exception callback, or PHP-SDK handlers would duplicate reports and violate the Laravel integration pattern.
handoff.forNextAgent: Error tracking for uncaught Laravel-reported exceptions is complete through config/posthog.php and package discovery. Do not add a custom exception callback or PostHog middleware. Handled exceptions may use PostHog\Laravel\Facades\PostHog::captureException only at intentional, relevant handling boundaries in future instrumentation work.
handoff.evidence: Read config/posthog.php and confirmed capture_exceptions is true. Read the Laravel SDK reference, which states that the Laravel SDK automatically captures exceptions reported through Laravel’s reportable exception path and that a manual PHP SDK report callback must not be added alongside it. No dependency installation, builds, tests, or app processes were run.
handoff.assumptions: Trusted the prior handoff that posthog/posthog-laravel 0.4.4 is installed and package discovery is active; this task did not re-verify upstream installation work.

handoff.goals: Choose high-value user actions, instrument them with attributable PostHog captures, and record the new analytics contract.
handoff.did: Created `.posthog-wizard-cache/.posthog-events.json` with four newly instrumented events. Updated `app/Http/Controllers/Site/OrderController.php` to capture `payment_proof_submitted` only after a valid InstaPay proof is stored, using payment method, proof-file presence, monetary value, and currency—no payment reference or customer data. Updated `app/Http/Controllers/Site/ReviewController.php` to capture `review_submitted` only when a new review is created, with rating and locale only—never review text or name. Updated `app/Http/Controllers/Admin/OrderController.php` to capture `order_status_updated` for actual single and bulk state transitions, and `payment_rejected` after the rejection succeeds. These admin captures use Laravel request context, so they are attributed to the authenticated administrator without manually repeating a distinct ID. Existing storefront funnel events and server-side `purchase`/`payment_verified` tracking were left intact to avoid duplicate instrumentation.
handoff.forNextAgent: The Laravel facade is now used for four new server events. Storefront proof and review requests are intentionally captured plainly/personlessly: this app has admin accounts, but its customers perform these signed-link actions without a stable authenticated identity or browser request-context header. Admin events capture plainly and inherit the authenticated admin from Laravel SDK request context. The event inventory contains only events introduced in this task; existing frontend ecommerce events remain implemented through `resources/js/lib/track.ts`.
handoff.evidence: Re-read all three edited controllers and the event inventory after editing. Verified each capture follows the successful action, event names are snake_case, no event property includes customer PII, and admin captures do not manually provide a distinct ID. No builds, linters, or tests were run, as required by the task.
handoff.assumptions: Assumed the prior initialization and identification steps remain active: `posthog/posthog-laravel` is package-discovered, request context resolves authenticated admins, and the configured Laravel PostHog facade flushes at request boundaries.

For a future AI instrumentation, the effective privacy setting should be documented at the configured wrapper/capture location, retain content capture by default unless requirements change, and can be changed according to https://posthog.com/docs/ai-observability/privacy-mode.

handoff.reportSection:
## Starter analytics dashboard

Created [Analytics basics (wizard)](https://us.posthog.com/project/757753/dashboard/2393268) with four 30-day daily trend tiles for payment proof submissions, submitted reviews, order-status updates, and rejected payments. The new order-status tile has begun receiving events; the other new streams will populate automatically as their corresponding actions occur.

handoff.goals: Configure PostHog log capture for the supported runtime using the matching documented platform setup, without exporting existing application logs.
handoff.did: Loaded the logs skill menu, installed and read the `logs-other` skill, then read its generic OTLP reference together with the Laravel integration commandments and example. Audited the Laravel 13 application’s Monolog configuration, server actions, queue job, command, existing PostHog SDK, and installed OpenTelemetry-related files. No files were changed. The available documentation has platform-specific implementations for Node, Python, Go, Java, and client SDKs, but no PHP/Laravel implementation or PHP-native PostHog log capture. Its generic other-languages page only directs users to select an OpenTelemetry client from that language’s ecosystem and provides protocol requirements; it does not document a PHP exporter API or a Laravel/Monolog integration pattern. Existing application logs therefore remain untouched, as required.
handoff.forNextAgent: Log capture is intentionally not configured. This is a Laravel 13/PHP server application, not a browser-only app, and no MCP server was found in the preceding workflow context. `config/logging.php` has only standard Laravel channels and no existing PostHog/OTLP export. The installed `posthog/posthog-php` package contains an optional tracing `OpenTelemetry/ContextSpanProcessor.php`, not a log exporter; no application OpenTelemetry setup was found. A future implementation needs a documented, version-compatible PHP OTLP logs exporter and an explicit Laravel/Monolog bridge. It must use a dedicated logger/exporter and emit only newly added, non-sensitive lines (for example after a successful order payment action), preserve all existing channels, read `POSTHOG_API_KEY` and `POSTHOG_HOST` from environment configuration, and avoid blocking request startup or delivery. Once configured, trigger the selected successful action and look for that dedicated line in PostHog Logs; delivery is unverified until observed. To export existing loggers later, attach the same exporter handler to the desired existing Laravel log channel—this was deliberately not done.
handoff.evidence: Read `.claude/skills/logs-other/SKILL.md`, `references/other.md`, and `references/start-here.md`. The generic reference explicitly directs language-specific SDK selection via the OpenTelemetry ecosystem registry and gives no PHP code/API; its supported-platform list does not include PHP or Laravel. Read `composer.json`, `config/logging.php`, relevant order actions, queue job, command, provider, and searched source/vendor/lockfile for existing OpenTelemetry or PostHog log exporters. `config/logging.php` contains no PostHog/OTLP channel, and vendor inspection found only the PostHog PHP SDK tracing context processor.
handoff.assumptions: Assumed the supplied installed documentation is the authoritative source for this task. No request, build, lint, test, or package installation was run because no documented PHP/Laravel log-capture implementation applies.
handoff.conflict: No documented PHP/Laravel OTLP log exporter integration was available, so adding an unverified exporter/Monolog bridge would violate the required documented-platform constraint.
